claims.text: The baseline elemental Cr coating on zirconium-alloy cladding is prone to interdiffusion-induced failure at elevated temperatures.
A 50–100 nm CrN layer can be introduced at the Cr/Zr-alloy interface by reactive sputtering during Cr deposition.
The resulting coating architecture is a Cr/CrN bilayer on a zirconium-alloy substrate.
An optimized 50–100 nm CrN interlayer will inhibit high-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion with the CrN interlayer will prevent premature coating failure during approximately 1200°C steam exposure for about 100 seconds.
The Cr/CrN coating will retain oxidation protection in subcritical water at approximately 300°C.
Adjusting the CrN layer thickness and composition can mitigate thermomechanical stresses that could cause delamination or cracking.
The proposed CrN diffusion barrier is thermodynamically stable at the stated service and accident conditions.
CrN exhibits sufficiently low atomic mobility to function as a Cr–Zr diffusion barrier.
Compositionally tailoring the CrN layer can minimize thermal-expansion mismatch and interfacial stress.
The CrN layer impedes atomic diffusion of Cr and Zr at elevated temperatures.
Reducing interdiffusion and interfacial stress will stabilize the interface, maintain adhesion, and prevent deleterious reactions leading to coating failure.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the Cr/CrN bilayer will show significantly reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the Cr/CrN bilayer will show enhanced adhesion after thermal exposure.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the Cr/CrN bilayer will sustain protective performance under both approximately 300°C subcritical water and approximately 1200°C steam for about 100 seconds.
The magnitude of improvement will depend on the tunable properties of the CrN barrier.
